newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat Italy Nov car registration fall 17 pct.
newsitem.headline: Fiat Italy Nov car registration fall 17 pct.

text.p: Italian carmaker Fiat showed a 17.1 percent fall in new car registrations in November to 61,150 from levels seen in November 1995. The figure covers all car marques owned by the Fiat Group.
Earlier, the Italian Ministry of Transport said that Italian new car registrations in November fell 11.44 percent to 134,000 from November 1995.

The Ministry of Transport data showed that new car registrations of the Fiat marque dropped 14.36 percent to 47,800, Alfa Romeo fell some 44.40 percent to 4,650, while Lancia-Autobianchi slipped 9.15 percent to 8,700 units.
For the month of November, Fiat group's share of the market fell to 45.63 percent from 48.75 percent in November 1995.

In the first 11 months of the year, the group Fiat has shown a fall in registrations of 4.42 percent to 712,917 with its share of the market falling to 43.82 percent from 45.69 percent in November 1995.
In the November new car figures, Mercedes saw registrations up 8.9 percent, BMW rose 7.22 percent, Ford was 19.3 percent higher, Rover rose 20.2 percent and Nissan was up 5.3 percent.

On the negative side in November, Opel fell 4.5 percent, Renault was off 5.6 percent, and Volvo down 6.8 percent. Especially poor figures came from Volkswagen down 27.6 percent and Peugeot off 38.7 percent.

From the beginning of 1996, new car registrations were positive in Italy for BMW up 22.3 percent, Ford was ahead 7.9 percent, Mercedes 18.3 percent higher, Rover was up 24.7 percent and Citroen rose 8.9 percent.
Showing net falls was Volvo off 14.9 percent, Saab down 26.7 percent, while smaller falls were seen for Volkswagen off 1.78 percent and Renault off 2.2 percent with Peugeot down 9.9 percent.
